MCGILL UNIVERSITY

McGill University is an English-language public research university located in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. Founded in 1821 by royal charter granted by King George IV, the university bears the name of James McGill, a Scottish merchant whose bequest in 1813 formed the university's precursor, University of McGill College (or simply, McGill College); the name was officially changed to McGill University in 1885.

McGill's main campus is on the slope of Mount Royal in downtown Montreal in the borough of Ville-Marie, with a second campus situated in Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, 30 kilometres (19 mi) west of the main campus on Montreal Island, and a third francophone medical campus in Gatineau, Quebec. The university is one of two members of the Association of American Universities located outside the United States, alongside the University of Toronto, and is the only Canadian member of the Global University Leaders Forum (GULF) within the World Economic Forum.

McGill offers degrees and diplomas in over 300 fields of study, with the highest average entering grades of any Canadian university. Most students are enrolled in the six largest faculties: Arts, Science, Medicine, Education, Engineering, and Management.


McGill is the most internationally diverse of any medical-doctoral research university in Canada, with international students comprising over 30% of its student population and hailing from more than 150 countries. Additionally, over 41% of students are born outside of Canada. McGill is ranked among the world's top universities by major educational publications and has held the top position in the country for the past 17 years in the annual Maclean's Canadian university rankings.

McGill counts among its alumni and faculty:

  • 12 Nobel laureates and 147 Rhodes Scholars (the most of any university in Canada)
  • 16 billionaires
  • The current Prime Minister, and two former Prime Ministers of Canada
  • Two Governors General of Canada
  • 15 Justices of the Supreme Court of Canada
  • At least eight foreign leaders and more than 100 members of national legislatures
  • 8 Academy Award winners, 10 Grammy Award winners, 13+ Emmy Award winners, 4 Pulitzer Prize winners
  • 121 Olympians with over 35 Olympic medals


The inventors of the game of basketball, modern organized ice hockey, and the pioneers of gridiron football, as well as the founders of several major universities and colleges, are also graduates of McGill.


Notable researchers include Ernest Rutherford, who discovered the atomic nucleus and conducted his Nobel Prize–winning research on the nature of radioactivity while working as Professor of Experimental Physics at the university. Other notable inventions by McGillians include the world's first artificial cell, web search engine, and charge-coupled device, among others.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline).

If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


Documents you will need to take with you:

  • Certified copies of the bachelor's degree and the transcript of the bachelor
  • CAQ and proof of obtaining a study permit

Please note: upon arrival, you will be asked to provide official copies of all transcripts and diplomas obtained (i.e. your baccalaureate diploma and transcript) at the Office of the Registrar.


To be given to Epitech bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


Additionally, please note that there are additional tuition fees on the side of the partner university that you need to take into account: 4200€ for French and Belgian students and 36 100€ for non-French and non-Belgian students.


2. Visa

The steps must be taken at the green light from McGill University, because the procedures can take a long time.


Check out updated information directly on the McGill website here:

https://www.mcgill.ca/continuingstudies/scs-future-students/international-students/quebec-caq-and-study-permits


Once you have your admission letter in hand, you must obtain:

  • the Quebec Acceptance Certificate for studies (CAQ), issued by the government of Quebec (At the expense of the student : 120$ CA)


The application of the Quebec Acceptance Certificate for studies must be done online and it takes approximatively 4 weeks to be issued.


The steps to apply for the CAQ:

Once you have received your admission letter, follow these steps and apply online:

  • Go to www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/en/electronic-services/caq-electronic/index.html
  • Complete the online CAQ application
  • Print:
  • declaration and commitment form (must be signed) and
  • the personalized checklist
  • Review and ensure you have the appropriate support documents – remember to include ALL pages of your Offer of Admission.
  • We boldly recommend that you mail your application package with all supporting documents by express mail to the address indicated on the personalized checklist.


Note: Whether you apply online or mail your application, you must mail the required documents to MIFI's Montréal office, regardless of your current place of residence. Your application will not be considered until all supporting documents have been received, so don't delay. Processing time is 4 to 6 weeks!

The bank letter in French will be required for the CAQ request (see corresponding paragraph below). As an indication, the amount requested in 2026 is 24 617 $ CAD.

Please follow the sample letter available by clicking here. For the tuition fees, you will pay those of Epitech. There are additional tuition fees on the side of the partner university that you need to take into account: 4200€ for French and Belgian students and 36 100€ for non-French and non-Belgian students.


PLEASE NOTE: if the bank letter is not in your name but that of your parents, for example, you must attach the declaration of financial support (you must also attach it for the CAQ request):

http://www.immigration-quebec.gouv.qc.ca/publications/fr/etudes/D09.pdf

  • the study permit, issued by Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada - IRCC (Cost to be borne by the student: 150 $ CA + 85$ for biometrics fee). Once you have received the electronic version of your CAQ, immediately apply for your Study Permit.


The application must be done online on the IRCC website.

This study permit application automatically includes a visa or Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) at no additional cost.


Apply online: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html


The IRCC website allow you to pay fees related to the study permit application, apply for the study permit, verify the status of your application.

The estimated time for the process is 12 weeks.


Go to this website to see the study permit application process:

Guide 5269 – Présenter une demande de permis d’études de l‘extérieur du Canada - Canada.ca


Citizens of all countries except the United States and other minor exceptions have to give their biometrics in order to obtain a visa or permit.


In the hours following submission of your online application, you will receive the 'instruction letter' in your MyCIC account with instructions to submit your biometrics at a collection service point. For more information, just click here:

https://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/information/ou-fournir-donnees-biometriques.asp


Students who reside or have resided for six months or more in the past year in certain countries need a medical exam by a IRCC-approved physician. You should allow at least one month for this process, and you are responsible for the cost of the exam. The embassy that handles your case will contact you and provide instructions as needed.

Citizens of certain countries must obtain a temporary resident visa (TRV) or electronic travel authorization (eTA) from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to be able to enter Canada. The visa is placed directly in your passport, whereas the eTA is electronically linked to your passport. Your application for a study permit made outside Canada automatically includes a visa or an eTA at no additional cost.


You will receive confirmation that the study permit has been issued, and you will have to queue at the immigration services at your point of entry into Canada to collect the study permit.


Note: when applying for a study permit, you must indicate the number of the designated educational institution (PST) of your university in Canada. You can find the PST for your institution on the following page:

http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/etudier/etudier-etablissements-liste.asp


Regarding the study permit, on the form to be completed (imm1294f) and to be provided on the Quebec immigration site, you are asked the level of study at this university: put 'University Baccalaureate'.


Upon receipt of the document, there you will also thoroughly check your number of Electronic Travel Authorization (AVE) appeared in the second paragraph of the second page. If it does not appear, you will have to make the request online via the following site:http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/visiter/ave.asp


The request is processed in 72 hours and the cost is $7.

Please note: obtaining the CAQ and Study Permit takes several months, which is why it is essential to start applying for the CAQ upon receipt of the letter of admission. In the absence of these documents, entry to the territory may be refused.


3. International insurance

You can find here some information about the health and hospitalization insurance from Laval University for international students


Enrolling in the health and hospitalization insurance plan for international students | Université Laval (ulaval.ca)

  • Basic social protection
  • There is a specific agreement between France and Quebec for basic social protection on site for students of French nationality. This agreement allows you to benefit from on-site support for your health expenses (up to the equivalent of French student social security).
  • The file will be to be created upon receipt of acceptance at the host university. The process can take several months. Proof of your affiliation with student social security in France will be required.


Before departure:

You will need to ask your health insurance company for the necessary supporting documents and the SE 401-Q-106 form. This form, already completed by the international relations department, can be found in the media of your international relations intranet. You must then send it to the CPAM of your residence in order to have it signed. The validated form which will be returned to you by the CPAM will certify that you will be insured under the social security system in France and will allow your affiliation in Quebec. (NB: upon receipt of the form, remember to check the validity period which will have been indicated by the CPAM. Any form which will not cover you for the full duration of your stay will imply a renewal of the process during the year).


Upon arrival in Quebec:

You will need to register with the Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec (RAMQ) by submitting this form.

You will therefore be able to access RAMQ health care benefits and benefit from health and maternity insurance. In the event of a work accident or occupational disease, you will be covered by the Commission de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CSST).


Please note: it will be important to present the RAMQ affiliation certificate to the Bureau du Registraire. Otherwise, the university will be legally required to bill you for its own international health insurance. Late fees may also be imposed on you if you do not send the affiliation certificate before the deadline given to you.


Social protection and complementary health

  • You must also take out international insurance (covering your medical and hospital costs on site, as well as repatriation).

Foreign students (other than French) must take out insurance for international students from McGill.


4. Help on arrival

If you arrive at Montréal-Trudeau airport in August (between August 4 and September 1), you can inquire about the "Accueil Plus" service, which allows you to reduce the waiting time for recover your study permit: http://www.accueilplus.ca/?lang=fr


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside of France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane.
accomodation: Students may request on-campus housing although it is available on a limited basis. Off-campus housing is also available. More information on costs is available on the McGill housing website, as well as some recommendations.
courses:
Students will participate in the Certificate of Management at the School of Continuing Studies at McGill, over three trimesters.

  • Fall: End of August – End of December
  • Spring (“Winter”): Beginning of January – End of April
  • Summer: May – August


The program is generally formatted as:

  • 4 classes in the fall
  • 4 in the spring/winter
  • 4 in the summer


Students must complete a total of 36 local credits over the course of the program.

Take into account this is Management focused with a lot of economics and mathematics.


Epitech will cover the tuition fees at McGill to the extent of the credits required according to the program followed. Any additional module you wish to take will be at your expense.
cost:
Students are responsible for the 4th year fees at EPITECH, as well as the program fee associated with this destination (the specific amount can be found in the application guide). EPITECH pays tuition to McGill on your behalf but you are responsible for housing, food, transport, international health insurance, etc.


You can find more information and compare cost of living in Montréal here:

https://www.jechoisismontreal.com/en/student-living-costs/montreal-vs-paris/?devise=CAD


Departure and costs relative to settling in:

  • Paris - Montréal round trip flights: around 800 euros
  • CAQ: 120$ CA
  • Study permit: 150$ CA
  • Adapted clothing for winter in Quebec: 500$ CA
  • Arrival (travel, temporary accommodation, restaurants): 450$ CA
  • Moving in costs (housing equipment, deposits…): 600$ CA

Living expenses:

  • Food: from 250$ CA to 350$ CA / month
  • Telephone, Internet, etc.: 40 to 70$ CA / month
  • Personal expenses, leisure, clothing, etc.: around 500$ / month
  • Other
These prices are for information only, they may vary.
